correctness.rationale: Replayed the trace gain directly by series/parallel effective resistances: the drop for a vertex pair is its squared clipped-ramp separation divided by d+1/w. Summing gives the centered variance and parity penalty. The all-span affine difference is positive at zero weight and, at W_n, its factorization is strictly positive except at tail sum t=2 (the t=1 parity case is separately positive). The slope for t=2 is negative beyond W_n; n<=8 has nonnegative slopes. Thus the only critical tie is the endpoint and {1,n-2}, with W_9=7/4. Sequential convergence of normalized gain, including d/n going to zero, and the unique maximum of x/4-x²/6 give the span and both normalized trace limits at every fixed w>0.
residual_risks: Uploaded code was not run; analytic replay supports the universal claim. No claim about all later finite-n transitions or w varying with n in the fixed-w limit.

value.rationale: This is a natural test of whether joining the largest-resistance pair optimizes a standard network objective: nine is the first possible counterexample size, with an exact conductance scale and the complete critical tie. The limiting geometry quantifies an appreciable one-eighth improvement in leading coherence cost versus the endpoint design. Both are usable design facts; no claim that optimizing spectral gap or multiple chords has been solved.
residual_risks: Practical interpretation depends on the unit undirected path and one fixed-price-by-placement conductance, not other network constraints.
